title: Store writer lock: flock on .mulch/.lock around load->mutate->save — parallel mulch processes silently lose records
description:
CONTEXT (2026-10-15, user request: port the seeds-0d7b writer lock to mulch):

- mulch (sprint-28 tree) does read-modify-write over .mulch/expertise/<domain>.jsonl (+ mulch.config.yaml for domain registration/auto-create) with NO inter-process exclusion: two mulch processes (two agents recording, record racing doctor --fix) both load, both rewrite_domain, the last rename wins and the other's records are silently lost (lost update). Same class as the fabro-4cfc tracker incident.
- The REFERENCE ml 0.10.7 has its own lock: utils/lock.ts withFileLock — PER-FILE O_CREAT|O_EXCL lockfile at `<file>.lock`, 50ms retry, 5s timeout (error: "Timed out waiting for lock on <path>. If no other mulch process is running, delete the lock file manually."), 30s mtime-staleness recovery, held around the whole read->dedupe->upsert->write cycle (record.ts:388ff); dry-run reads run lock-free; hooks fire outside the lock. move.ts even nests target+source locks (deadlock-prone ordering).
- Weakness of the reference form (why we deviate): a crashed holder leaves the lockfile — writers wedge up to 30s or until manual deletion; the staleness-steal can in principle double-admit a >30s holder. seeds (denkhaus/seeds, seeds-0d7b, shipped in seeds 0.8.0) solved exactly this store-wide with flock: advisory exclusive lock on .seeds/.lock via std::fs::File::try_lock, kernel-owned (released on process death — no stale-lockfile machinery), 5s acquire timeout, 25ms poll, Error::LockTimeout, Store::open_exclusive acquires BEFORE the first read and holds until drop. Proven code: crates/seeds/src/lock.rs + tests/writer_lock.rs (8 parallel creates keep every record; holder death proceeds immediately; reads never create the lock file).

DEMAND:
1. Port the seeds WriterLock as a LIB module (mulch::lock): advisory exclusive flock on `.mulch/.lock` (create + !truncate, permanent zero-byte sibling), acquired BEFORE the store's first read, held until the StoreFiles drops — the whole load->mutate->save cycle of a mutating command is atomic against other mulch processes. Store-wide granularity deliberately: one lock covers domain file + config mutations as one transaction (the reference's per-file lock leaves the domain auto-create config race open) and sidesteps move's nested-lock ordering.
2. Mutating commands open exclusive: record (incl. batch/stdin; --dry-run stays lock-free like the reference), edit, outcome, add, delete, delete-domain, move, doctor --fix (report mode stays lock-free), init (uniform). Reads (status, validate, render surfaces) stay lock-free and never create .mulch/.lock.
3. Bounded wait: 5s (25ms poll), then fail fast — plain error naming the lock path + json failure envelope, exit 1 (wording is a DEVIATION, see 4).
4. README DEVIATIONS bullet: kernel-owned flock on store-wide .mulch/.lock instead of the reference's per-file O_EXCL lockfiles with 30s staleness recovery; different timeout error; cross-domain writers serialize. Rationale: crash-safety — a dead writer cannot wedge the store, no stale-lockfile machinery (the seeds-0d7b lesson).
5. .mulch/.lock hygiene: init writes `.mulch/.gitignore` (`*.lock`) via write_missing (deviation: reference init writes no such file); existing stores add the ignore once by hand (this repo does it in this sprint). Verify the deviation is INVISIBLE to the reference: run the reference ml validate/doctor/status on a store with .mulch/.lock + .mulch/.gitignore present and pin byte-identical output vs a clean store.
6. Fabro note: the lock lives in the LIB seam (StoreFiles exclusive open), so fabro's embedded mutations get the same protection.

ACCEPTANCE:
- tests/writer_lock.rs (CLI level, port from seeds): 8 parallel `mulch record` on one fresh store -> all 8 records present, ids unique, no lost update; while a helper process holds the lock, a second record fails fast within the timeout and succeeds after release; a SIGKILLed holder -> next mutating command proceeds immediately; read commands never create .mulch/.lock while record does.
- lib unit tests in lock.rs: timeout, drop-release, waiter-handoff (port seeds' three).
- Battery stays byte-identical for single-process runs (no lock residue in twin stores); init battery gains the .gitignore deviation pin; doctor orphan/file-anchors surfaces must not flag .mulch/.lock or the .gitignore.
- Gates: nextest (workspace) + fmt + clippy -D warnings + just qualitygate green.
